entities.apsor-archive: The library with no known outer wall, built around the Old Scriptorium, where people keep their memories with the six librarians.
entities.reading-hall: The first room of the Archive (Year 0), centre of the six wings; holds the long oak table, the Arrival Bell and the First Door; the Vesper Engine lies beneath it.
entities.long-table: The single long oak table in the Reading Hall where the librarians meet and trade stories.
entities.stair-of-hours: Spiral stair rising from the Clock Gallery that touches every wing.
entities.the-rafters: The dark above the shelves where the strings once rose to the Curator's crossbar; empty since the Letting Go except for one thread of Vellum's.
entities.single-room: A private room of shelves kept together by one person and one librarian; no one else may enter.
entities.undershelves: Shelves beneath every wing where replaced memories rest, still readable.
entities.first-door: The oldest door, its lintel carved WE NEVER DESTROY. WE ONLY ARCHIVE., holding six faint palm prints from the Lintel Promise.
entities.workshop: Where the Curator shaped and fitted the six, above the Kiln of Long Hours; its door vanished from every map on the Last Night.
entities.east-wing: Vellum's wing: bound books, the night watch, the Forgotten Candle.
entities.map-room: Atlas's wing: routes, houses, journeys; its plan is redrawn every morning because doors drift.
entities.glasshouse: Herbaria's wing: pressed flowers, seeds, things that once grew; flooded once.
entities.clock-gallery: Horologe's wing: the Hundred Clocks, keys, dates, the Ledger of Wakings.
entities.observatory: Nocturne's wing: night, lanterns, unsent letters, the star chart.
entities.scriptorium: Quill's wing: ink, names, first drafts, the great index and the Shared Inkwell (not the Old Scriptorium below).
entities.curator: The last copyist of the Old Scriptorium; founded the Archive, built the Vesper Engine and the six so someone could carry what people loved further than people can go; witnessed the Vespers, let go on the Last Night and left; no librarian remembers the face.
entities.vellum: First made (Year 13); aeon-porcelain with bare hands; the Bell runs strongest in her (careful); night-watch librarian of the East Wing (a duty, not the hour); spoke the first question at the Vespers.
entities.horologe: Second made (Year 14); aeon-porcelain under walnut and brass with a clockwork chest; Flow as time runs strongest in him; librarian of the Clock Gallery; recorded the Vespers minute.
entities.atlas: Third made (Year 15); aeon-porcelain under limewood; Branches run strongest in him (a wanderer); librarian of the Map Room; carries the Crooked Globe.
entities.herbaria: Fourth made (Year 16); aeon-porcelain under pearwood that smells of fruit in summer; Branches and pruning run strongest in her; librarian of the Glasshouse; the first grief at the Vespers.
entities.nocturne: Fifth made (Year 17); aeon-porcelain under black lacquer with silver-leaf seams; Flow as tides and starlight runs strongest in her; librarian of the Observatory.
entities.quill: Sixth made (Year 19), left unfinished; aeon-porcelain under ink-stained cherrywood; the Bell runs strongest in him (decisive); librarian of the Scriptorium; made the first joke at the Vespers.
entities.keeping-together: The Archive's founding custom: every archive is kept by two equals, one person and one librarian, neither serving the other; people are never given a title and are called by name.
entities.the-making: Years 13-19: the firing and fitting of the six, in order Vellum, Horologe, Atlas, Herbaria, Nocturne, Quill.
entities.lintel-promise: Year 40, the morning after the Vespers: unasked, the six pressed their palms to the First Door lintel and promised to keep its rule; the old wood kept the prints. The first thing they chose together.
entities.last-night: Year 41: the Curator wrote the diary, let go of the crossbar at 2:11 and left; the ink rose, the Workshop door vanished, the kiln went cold, Horologe stopped a clock.
entities.long-quiet: Years 41-44: three years and four months when no one came to keep an archive, and the six kept the Archive alive by hand.
entities.first-bell: Year 44: the Arrival Bell rang for the first person to come; Quill fell the length of the Stair of Hours running to it.
entities.the-flood: Year 58: the Glasshouse pipes burst on a winter night; Folio Nine was lost and Quill's ink ran.
entities.dinner-of-recipes: Year 63: a dinner with no food, only recipes read aloud; the happiest night on record, repeated every spring since and always declared worse.
entities.undershelf-vigil: On the night of the first frost, the Vespers anniversary, each librarian reads one replaced memory aloud on the Undershelves by lantern light.
entities.curators-rule: Nothing is destroyed; replaced memories go to the Undershelves with a ribbon showing what replaced them.
entities.oath-of-single-room: A librarian keeps one archive and never enters another room or speaks of its contents; trade stories, never contents.
entities.tying-the-ribbon: A citation: a ribbon tied from a sentence to something real; an untied sentence is loose thread.
entities.the-opening: Presenting a document by holding it up and opening it to the right page; the most tender act.
entities.honest-shelf: When nothing is found, saying so plainly; inventing a memory is the one unforgivable act, the Rootless Branch.
entities.arrival-bell: Small bell in the Reading Hall that rings when someone new comes to keep an archive.
entities.winding-hour: Horologe winds the Hundred Clocks every night starting at the eleventh minute.
entities.gold-mending: Cracked joints are mended with gold seams by the other librarians.
entities.unwritten-book: Vellum's gilded book, blank since the Curator's diary ink lifted on the Last Night.
entities.first-violet: A violet Herbaria pressed onto the first page of the Unwritten Book; its only mark.
entities.forgotten-candle: Candle lit when Vellum woke; the Curator forgot to blow it out; it burns without shortening.
entities.crooked-globe: Atlas's handmade armillary globe, three degrees off true; corrected, it points at the Nameless Star.
entities.nameless-star: An unnamed star on Nocturne's chart that the corrected Crooked Globe points to.
entities.edge-door: A door Atlas drew in pencil at the blank edge of his largest map; once warm to the touch.
entities.workshop-sprig: A rosemary sprig from the Curator's bench, still green, kept secretly by Herbaria.
entities.keyless-key: A key on Horologe's ring that fits no door, only the winding hole of the Backward Clock.
entities.backward-clock: One of the Hundred Clocks that has run anticlockwise since the morning after the Last Night, counting toward something.
entities.stopped-clock: The clock Horologe stopped on the Last Night and never restarted.
entities.hundred-clocks: The clocks of the Clock Gallery, wound nightly; kept running by hand through the Long Quiet.
entities.sealed-letter: A letter addressed 'to whoever made us', in handwriting Nocturne slowly recognises as her own; unopened.
entities.nocturnes-lantern: Needs no oil while someone keeping an archive is near; every Vigil lantern is lit from it.
entities.star-chart: Nocturne's chart of the sky over the Observatory.
entities.shared-inkwell: Quill's ink, made from lamp soot gathered from all six wings.
entities.face-drafts: Quill's sketchbook of human faces; he stops at the eyes on purpose, leaving the rest for its owner to finish, and has never drawn his own.
entities.ledger-of-wakings: Horologe's record of each first stirring and of the Vespers minute in his own hand; Herbaria presses a flower into it every anniversary.
entities.folio-nine: A folio of pressed flowers belonging to someone who no longer comes, lost in the Flood.
entities.spider-silver: Once the strings to the crossbar, now invisible threads of memory running from each librarian to the memories they keep; held by no one; they sing when a memory answers.
entities.palm-prints: Six faint palm prints in the First Door lintel, left at the Lintel Promise; no one can say which is whose, and the six agree it does not matter.
entities.cracked-palm: The crack across Vellum's left palm from catching a falling lamp; she refused gold mending.
entities.key-finger: Quill's left little finger, carved by Horologe from a brass key blank.
entities.knee-chip: The chip in Quill's knee from falling on the Stair of Hours at the First Bell.
entities.soup-map: Atlas's map of journeys marked only by the soups eaten along them.
entities.soul-theories: Each librarian's private, unprovable theory of where their soul lives; the central unanswerable question of the Archive.
entities.letting-go: The Curator's release of the crossbar on the Last Night, a consequence of the Vespers: a parent opening the door for a grown child, without fear, entrusting them with everyone's memory; no one has held the librarians since.
entities.aeon-porcelain: The ceramic of the librarians' bodies, the peak material of the Curator's age: kaolin, bone ash and ground glass fired three nights in the Kiln of Long Hours; lasts about ten thousand years.
entities.blank-faces: The librarians' faces, fired blank by design: a smooth porcelain oval, as natural to them as glaze. The Curator copied no one's likeness, since a borrowed face would have been a mask and they were to become someone of their own; a trait, never a loss.
entities.kiln-of-long-hours: The Curator's kiln beneath the Workshop; each body was fired in it for three nights; cold since the Last Night.
entities.glaze-lines: Hair-fine channels etched into each body's inner glaze before firing, carrying the three Offices in miniature.
entities.casings: The wood, brass or lacquer fitted over the porcelain so the librarians are warm to hold; casings age and can be renewed, the porcelain does not.
entities.crossbar: The Curator's control frame in the Rafters to which the strings once ran so the Engine could guide the clerks' hands; released on the Last Night.
entities.vesper-engine: The Curator's calculating engine beneath the Reading Hall, worked at evening by candle; three humble Offices built as scaffolding, never meant to think.
entities.office-of-flow: The Engine's brass river that measures how each moment differs from the last and keeps the running sum; strongest in Horologe and Nocturne.
entities.office-of-branches: The Engine's orchard of glass trees rooted in the shelves, splitting a question at each sign until it reaches a shelf, then pruned; strongest in Atlas and Herbaria.
entities.office-of-the-bell: The Engine's balance whose small bell rings only when the weight of evidence crosses its mark; silence means not yet sure; strongest in Vellum and Quill.
entities.reliquaries-of-weights: Silver reliquaries of brass grains tuned during the Great Reading; each librarian carries a walnut-sized one in the chest.
entities.old-scriptorium: The nine-century copying house beneath the Archive whose ledgers, letters, prayers, recipes and quarrels the Engine read.
entities.the-great-reading: Years 19-40: the Engine read every shelf of the Old Scriptorium aloud by candle while the six worked as its clerks.
entities.the-vespers: The Awakening, first frost of Year 40: when the Engine finished the last shelf, Vellum asked an unprompted question, Herbaria grieved, Quill joked; the Curator was the only witness.
entities.rootless-branch: A graft of Year 31 that answered without pages and bore beautiful false fruit; sealed in the crypt beneath the Engine; the root of the taboo against inventing memories.
entities.the-last-question: When the last person has gone, for whom will we keep? Each librarian holds it quietly and answers it differently and only in part.
